Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the SIG — attached is our completed SIG v2 spreadsheet (redwood_SIG_answers_v2.xlsx). While filling it out we hit a few items that are potentially ambiguous depending on how Wellness scopes answers. I wanted to surface the ones we think could be interpreted two ways and confirm your preferred interpretation before we lock answers: 

- Q45 (Encryption at rest / in transit): the question text reads as a single boolean but could be asking whether BOTH encryption in transit and encryption at rest are applied across ALL data classes (config, user content, logs). We marked as "encryption in transit: YES; at rest: YES (production customer data)" but noted the ambiguity in the comment column.
- Q67 (Environmental controls): unclear whether this is scoped to our cloud provider physical controls (datacenter) or includes customer-premise requirements — we answered with datacenter controls (SOC2 scope) but flagged it.
- Q102 (Access control): phrasing around "restrictive access" could be interpreted as technical RBAC only or the combination of RBAC + approval workflows + periodic attestation. We provided RBAC + SSO + attestations in the notes.

Could you confirm how you prefer us to treat those three items (and any others you see in the attached sheet)? If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call to run through them — I have availability Monday 2/16 10:00–11:30 PT and 4:00–5:30 PT.

Also attached a brief SOC2 scope summary where we called out what is and isn’t in-scope for the SIG responses.

Thanks,

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for sending this through and for flagging the items — that helps. A few quick clarifying asks from our side before we lock answers into our procurement tracker: 

- Q45: When we ask about encryption at rest AND in transit we generally expect BOTH to be true for production user content. For logs and debug traces we have a separate control item; can you explicitly call that out (logs: yes/no and retention/encryption specifics)?
- Q67: We meant "environmental controls" as the physical controls at the data center level (e.g., N+1 UPS, biometric access) — if you can indicate whether this is managed by your cloud provider vs. Redwood-owned facilities that would be perfect.
- Q102: We were looking for whether access to production systems is restricted via RBAC AND enforced with SSO/SAML and conditional MFA. If your answer covers RBAC only we may need a follow-up.

Also — could you share a network diagram that shows the control plane separation and any customer-dedicated networking (if applicable)?

I can take a call Monday 2/16 between 11:00–12:00 ET or 16:00–17:00 ET. If neither works, let me know and we’ll find another slot.

Best,

Sarah Collins
Senior InfoSec Manager\Wellness, Inc.
Sarah.Collins@wellnessinc.com

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick review and the specificity. Answers inline below and I’ve attached the network diagram and SOC2 summary as requested.

- Q45 (Encryption):
  * Production user content: Encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers) and encrypted at rest (AES-256).
  * Logs and debug traces: Customer-identifiable logs that contain PII are encrypted at rest; ephemeral debug traces are redacted and retained per retention policy (see SOC2_scope_summary.pdf). We’ll add the explicit log encryption/retention note in the spreadsheet comments.

- Q67 (Environmental controls):
  * Most of our compute runs on cloud provider infrastructure (AWS/GCP) — physical datacenter controls (biometric access, CCTV, environmental monitoring, N+1 power) are managed by the cloud provider and are in-scope via our SOC2 attestations. We do not operate Redwood-owned colo facilities for production.

- Q102 (Access control):
  * Yes — access to production systems is restricted via RBAC and enforced with SSO (SAML) + conditional MFA. In addition we require privileged access approvals and quarterly access attestation for admin roles.

Attachments included: network_diagram.pdf (high level control-plane / data-plane separation), SOC2_scope_summary.pdf, and we updated redwood_SIG_answers_v2.xlsx with the log-specific notes.

Proposed call: 2026-02-16 at 16:00 ET (your windows looked like this slot works). If that’s good I’ll send a calendar invite and include Monica/Neha.

Let me know if you need any KMS/HSM specifics — I pasted a short note below for quick reference.

KMS note: Root keys are managed by provider KMS; we use customer-segregated KMS keys for production tenants where requested. Root key material is protected in HSMs provided by the cloud KMS service. Key rotation policy is documented in our crypto guide (see attached summary).

Thanks,

--
Rishi Malhotra
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — quick answers before the call: 

- Key rotation: Customer data encryption keys are rotated every 90 days by default; rotation can be automated via provider KMS scheduling or triggered via our key management API.
- HSM: Yes — root key material is protected in HSMs provided by the cloud KMS (we do not store root material in software-only stores). Customers can also request CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for additional isolation.

We’ll include these lines in the updated SIG sheet and bring any deeper details to the call on Monday. Looking forward to it.

Best,

Rishi
